mechanism_inventory: stale accounting snapshot — settleUserBalance reads rebalancePositionBase/Quote and lastNumRebalance without first settling accrued interest, so the delta it computes may be stale relative to the current fee growth index

reward / index update ordering — updateRebalanceInterestGrowth must run before settleUserBalance to ensure rebalanceInterestGrowthBase/Quote reflects current block; if settleUserBalance is called first, users receive wrong rebalance interest

missing invariant enforcement — reallocate does not guard against totalAmount==0 (distinct from totalLiquidityAmount==0); if totalAmount is zero but borrowedAmount > 0, downstream ratio arithmetic (borrowedAmount / totalAmount) will revert or be skipped, leaving borrow positions unserviced

wrong lifecycle ordering — reallocate increments numRebalance and updates tick range before updateRebalanceInterestGrowth is called for the old range; the growth accumulators are therefore computed against the new (post-rebalance) position sizes rather than the old ones, permanently mis-accounting accrued interest

precision / packing / normalization edge — updateRebalanceInterestGrowth divides by lastRebalanceTotalSquartAmount (scaled by 1e18) using integer division; if lastRebalanceTotalSquartAmount is very large or the numerator is small, truncation to zero permanently loses accrued interest for all rebalance position holders

external-call failure / DoS — rebalanceForInRange calls IUniswapV3Pool.burn then .collect then .mint in sequence; a revert in any of these (e.g. mint reverts due to slippage or pool manipulation) leaves the position in a partially-burned state with no recovery path, permanently locking LP funds

value exceeds a logical / economic bound — settleUserBalance transfers deltaPositionUnderlying / deltaPositionStable from the shared rebalancePositionBase/Quote to the individual user position without checking whether the shared rebalance pool has sufficient balance, potentially pushing the shared pool into a negative (under-collateralised) state

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: reward / index update ordering: settleUserBalance is callable without first invoking updateRebalanceInterestGrowth, so a user's rebalance entry is settled against a stale rebalanceInterestGrowthBase/Quote accumulator, short-changing or over-paying their rebalance interest
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: any user who calls the public-facing function that invokes settleUserBalance before interest growth is updated for the current block; ordering is not enforced on-chain
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker opens a sqrtPerp position in a pair. 2. Interest accrues but updateRebalanceInterestGrowth has not been called this block. 3. Attacker calls settleUserBalance (directly or via a trade that triggers it) before the interest update. 4. updateRebalanceEntry computes delta using the stale rebalanceInterestGrowthBase/Quote. 5. Attacker's basePosition / stablePosition is credited with an incorrect (under- or over-counted) rebalance amount. 6. Other users who settle later receive the complementary error, netting a loss.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: other liquidity providers / rebalance position holders whose accrued interest is under-credited
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: attacker (if they receive over-credited interest) or the protocol (if the user is under-credited and the difference sits in the shared pool unclaimable)
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: source confirms there is no enforced ordering between updateRebalanceInterestGrowth and settleUserBalance; the accumulator (_sqrtAssetStatus.rebalanceInterestGrowthBase) is read inside updateRebalanceEntry without an in-function update call

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: wrong lifecycle ordering in reallocate: numRebalance is incremented and tick range updated (via Reallocation.getNewRange inside rebalanceForInRange) before updateRebalanceInterestGrowth is called for the old range, so the growth accumulators are applied to the post-rebalance position sizes rather than the pre-rebalance ones
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: any actor who triggers a rebalance (permissionless via reallocate if exposed) at a moment when the old range has accrued fee/premium growth; the mis-accounting is systemic and affects all position holders
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. LP range drifts out of threshold. 2. Anyone calls the function that invokes reallocate. 3. rebalanceForInRange burns old position, mints new one, sets new tickLower/tickUpper. 4. saveLastFeeGrowth is called capturing fees for the NEW range. 5. If updateRebalanceInterestGrowth is subsequently called, it uses lastRebalanceTotalSquartAmount (which may now reflect the post-rebalance state) against the old accumulated fees, computing wrong per-share growth. 6. All rebalance position holders have permanently incorrect interest credited.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: all holders of rebalancePositionBase / rebalancePositionQuote — their accrued interest before the rebalance is mis-allocated
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: the discrepancy sits in the shared pool or benefits later settlers at the expense of earlier ones
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: source shows rebalanceForInRange modifies tickLower/tickUpper and calls saveLastFeeGrowth before any interest settlement; the ordering flaw is directly visible in the code

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: missing balance check in settleUserBalance: the function debits deltaPositionUnderlying from _pairStatus.sqrtAssetStatus.rebalancePositionBase and credits it to _userStatus.basePosition with no guard that the shared rebalance pool holds sufficient balance, allowing the shared pool to go negative (under-collateralised)
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: an attacker with a large sqrtPerp position who calls settleUserBalance when the rebalance pool has been depleted by prior settlements or a manipulated rebalance, pulling more value than the pool holds
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker accumulates a large sqrtPerp position. 2. Other users settle first, draining rebalancePositionBase. 3. Attacker calls settleUserBalance; deltaPositionUnderlying is computed from their position size. 4. updatePosition is called with -deltaPositionUnderlying on the shared pool even if it goes negative. 5. Shared pool balance is negative; subsequent settlers cannot recover their share.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: subsequent rebalance position holders who can no longer withdraw their share
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: attacker extracts more than their pro-rata share of the rebalance pool
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: source shows no balance check before the updatePosition calls in settleUserBalance; the shared rebalancePositionBase/Quote can be driven negative by sequential calls

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: precision / packing / normalization edge — division by lastRebalanceTotalSquartAmount in updateRebalanceInterestGrowth may truncate interest to zero for small fee amounts or very large pool sizes
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: line: rebalanceInterestGrowthBase += settleUserFee(...) * 1e18 / int256(lastRebalanceTotalSquartAmount); no rounding-up or minimum check
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether the truncation is large enough in practice to constitute a material loss for any user, or whether it is dust-level; depends on runtime values of pool size and fee accrual rate
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: rebalance position holders who accrue interest in blocks where truncation rounds to zero
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: the shared pool retains the truncated amount (unclaimable)

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: external-call failure / DoS — rebalanceForInRange calls burn/collect/mint in sequence; a revert in mint (e.g. due to Uniswap callback manipulation or pool state) leaves the pool with liquidity permanently withdrawn and not re-deposited
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: rebalanceForInRange lines: burn -> collect -> mint, no try/catch or recovery path
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether the Uniswap V3 pool can be manipulated to cause mint to revert while burn has already succeeded, and whether this constitutes a permanent lock of LP funds or merely a transient revert of the entire transaction (which would revert burn too)
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: all LP depositors if the rebalance is permanently stuck
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: attacker who can cause the DoS

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: missing invariant enforcement on totalAmount==0 causing division-by-zero or revert
rejected_mechanisms.claimed_locus: totalAmount in SqrtPerpAssetStatus used in borrowedAmount/totalAmount ratio
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: within the visible source of reallocate and settleUserBalance, there is no division by totalAmount; the guard 'if (_assetStatus.totalAmount == 0) return;' in updateFeeAndPremiumGrowth (visible at bottom of source) protects the one location where totalAmount is used as a divisor in the visible code
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: the zero-totalAmount guard is present and causes an early return rather than a division; no revert or accounting mis-step results from this path in the visible source
rejected_mechanisms.leans_on_unproven_guard: false — the guard is directly visible in the source

impact_direction.attacker_receives: over-credited rebalance interest (mechanism 1) or excess pool balance (mechanism 3)
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: their principal sqrtPerp position while extracting value from the shared rebalance pool
impact_direction.victim_loses: other LP / rebalance position holders lose correctly-owed rebalance interest or their pro-rata share of the rebalance pool
impact_direction.invariant_violated: the invariant that sum(user rebalance interest credits) == total rebalance interest earned is violated by stale-index settlement; the invariant that rebalancePositionBase >= 0 (pool solvency) is violated by unbounded withdrawal in settleUserBalance
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: the loss is borne by third-party LPs, not the attacker's own funds; the mechanism is permissionless (any user can trigger settleUserBalance by trading or directly); the impact scales with position size and interest accrual, not dust
